title: Islam Lands
subtitle: Nubia, the Sudan, Tunisia and Algeria
summary: Michael Myers Shoemaker (1853–1924), an American traveller, made this journey about 1909; he dedicates the book to his wife, his companion on “our wanderings.” From Assouan they go up the Nile through Nubia to Abu-Simbel and on by train to Khartoum and Omdurman, where they meet Slatin Pasha and Father Ohrwalder; long chapters tell the history of the Mahdi, the Khalifa, and General Gordon. They return by Port Sudan and Suez to Cairo, which he compares with the Cairo he knew in 1873, and then go by motor car through Tunisia and Algeria: Tunis and Carthage, Karawan, Dougga, Constantine, Biskra, Timgad, the Kabyle mountains, and Algiers. With photographs and a plan of the palace at Khartoum.
